entry.content:
Miguel Galluzzi built the first Monster prototype on his holidays in 1991, bolting a 900 cc engine into the frame of an 851 superbike. The Dark goes back to that raw idea. Dark Stealth black covers the bodywork and wheels, while the front frame, intake cap and silencer stay bare. The 890 cc V2 makes 111 horsepower, and the whole bike weighs 386 pounds without fuel. Cornering ABS, traction control and wheelie control come standard, and the seat sits 32.1 inches off the ground.

entry.content:
On this 187-foot Heesen superyacht, light shapes the design of every room, the oval staircase a central showpiece of this approach.The spiral climbs four decks to a skylight, circling a 33-foot stack of thin blue metal tubes. Hidden lights trace the curve of every room, leather ribs on the columns glow from behind, and a raised parquet floor called Kimono carries a wave pattern. On the upper deck, the owner's suite faces forward onto a terrace of about 2,100 square feet that also works as a helipad for touch-and-go landings. Twin MTU engines push the aluminum hull to 18 knots, and six cabins sleep 12 guests, looked after by a crew of 13.

entry.content:
Classic. It says it right there in the name. And with spartan use of Arabic numerals on its matte black dial, a black NATO strap, and a single lumen dot on the black aluminum bezel insert, the Unimatic UC3 Classic does qualify. Pale green Super-LumiNova C3 markings ensure legibility, which is necessary when taking advantage of the 40mm brushed stainless steel case's 300m water resistance. It's powered by a Seiko Meca-quartz movement, which runs the phantom ladder hour and minute hands as well as the sweeping lollipop second hand. Made in Italy, each watch is individually numbered.
